subject: Recap: Spend cap constraints & batching roadmap
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@clearpay.com>; Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@clearpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T20:12:00Z
Subject: Recap: Spend cap constraints & batching roadmap

Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. Short recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points you called out:
- Bursty inference at month end; peaks ~3-4x baseline and sensitive to p99 latency.
- Current vendor spend climbing unpredictably (no caching, per-request model selection).
- Procurement preference for a capped pilot (<= $10k/mo) before larger commit.

Goals we discussed:
- 6-week technical pilot: validate latency SLOs (target p99 < 250ms), measure real token burn, and quantify UX regressions (if any) from caching/quantization.
- Show a credible path to 40–60% unit cost reduction using batching + prefix/KV caching for your conversational flows.

Initial sizing (your baseline traffic sample):
- Rough baseline: ~4.0B generated tokens/month (current setup, no caching).
- Typical per-request generation: 600–1,200 tokens (mix of short prompts + long-context summaries).

Levers we can apply and expected direction of impact (ballpark):
- Dynamic batching (latency-aware): reduces GPU time per token, typical savings 20–35% depending on latency window.
- Prefix / KV caching for repeated prompts: can cut generation tokens by 25–45% on your conversational flows.
- Quantized model variants (8-bit / 4-bit): reduces cost per token by ~10–20% with small quality tradeoffs to validate.

Ballpark pilot pricing options (to inform procurement):
- Conservative (no optimizations): est $22k–28k/mo.
- With batching only: est $14k–19k/mo.
- With batching + caching: est $9k–13k/mo.

Proposal / next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive next week (Marissa to lead) to lock latency windows and KV TTLs — blocks: 60–90 mins.
2) I’ll send a short SOW + cost breakdown (attached) for a capped pilot.
3) You share a 24–48 hour representative usage sample so we can tighten numbers (anonymous is fine).

Attachments: pilot-sow.pdf (SOW draft).

If that aligns, I’ll update the SOW to set a pilot cap and optional commitment discounts.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@clearpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@clearpay.com>
Date: 2028-03-21T21:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: Spend cap constraints & batching roadmap

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. Two quick clarifications and an ask:

1) Procurement tolerance for the pilot is around $8k–10k/mo (we can flex up for a short term if we see solid improvements).
2) We need a line-item showing expected delta from caching specifically (we run a lot of repeated prompts across onboarding flows).

I attached a small usage sample for a recent 48h window (monthly-usage-sample.csv) — it has request timestamps and approximate tokens. Can you use that to produce scenario numbers showing expected monthly spend at the pilot cap?

If you can get a firm cost sheet by tomorrow, I’ll run it with procurement.

Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering, ClearPay
liam@clearpay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@clearpay.com>
Cc: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@clearpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T01:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: Spend cap constraints & batching roadmap

On Wed, Mar 21, 2028 at 20:12, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for taking the time today — good conversation. Short recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned.

Appreciate the sample — used it to tighten up three scenario lines. High-level (monthly):

- Scenario A — No optimizations (baseline): ~4.0B gen tokens => est spend $24,800/mo.
- Scenario B — Batching engaged (latency window 100–200ms): ~30% lower GPU token cost => est spend $17,400/mo.
- Scenario C — Batching + Prefix caching (estimated cache hit 40% from sample): ~55% lower token generation => est spend $11,160/mo.

Interpretation relative to your $8k–10k pilot cap:
- With a $10k cap we can validate batching + caching but will need conservative cache-hits (we used 40% in Scenario C). If actual cache hits are higher you’ll come in under cap.
- We can structure the SOW to include: a hard pilot spend cap ($10k), a single-week overage window with prior notice, and conversion/discount terms if you commit to a 6–12 month reserved capacity afterwards.

Attached: clearpay-pilot-cost-breakdown.xlsx (line-item math), updated pilot-sow.pdf.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Schedule tech deep-dive (I’m proposing Thu 03/23 16:00 ET; calendar link in the SOW).
2) If procurement signs the cap, we’ll kick pilot within 7 business days after PO.
3) During pilot: weekly metric snapshot (tokens, cache hit rate, p50/p95/p99 latency).

Let me know whether the $10k cap is workable; if not we’ll sketch a tighter scope to match $8k.

Thanks — I’ll be on the call for the deep-dive and Marissa will lead the engineering runbook.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@clearpay.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T04:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: Spend cap constraints & batching roadmap

Looping in a couple of implementation pointers so expectations are clear before the tech call: 

- Latency SLOs: We can hold p99 < 250ms for the majority of requests with batching window ~150ms and an intermediate fast-path for short requests. We’ll validate on your sample traffic.
- Cache model: Prefix/KV cache with TTL options (30s, 5m, 1h). For onboarding flows TTL ~5m is typical and gives good hit rates without stale content risk.
- Data handling: Redwood supports customer-controlled retention + KMS for keys. If ClearPay requires zero retention we can disable persistent logs for the pilot (export-only audit).

Success criteria (pilot):
1) Achieve >= 40% reduction in billed generation tokens relative to baseline, OR
2) Demonstrate end-to-end cost per active user reduced by >= 35% while meeting p99 latency target.

I attached a short KPIs doc (pilot-kpis.md) and a checklist for the tech call. On the call we’ll also confirm telemetry hooks we need (per-route token counts, cache-hit rate, GPU utilization).

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@clearpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@clearpay.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: Spend cap constraints & batching roadmap

Thanks all — that level of detail helps a lot. Procurement is comfortable with a $10k hard cap for an initial 6-week pilot with the reporting cadence you suggested. Two asks before PO:

1) Please add an explicit line that we can disable persistent retention for the pilot.
2) Include the preferred rollback plan if latency or UX regressions exceed the SLO for more than 48 hours.

I’ll route the SOW and the cost sheet to procurement now. Targeting a PO by Friday EOD if they don’t have additional questions. I’ll confirm the exact PO number once it’s issued.

Liam
